result.summary:
Focused re-gate of the single correction ordered in step-07b. Verified via `git show 75184403` (the commit step-07c's edit landed in) rather than trusting CODE-DESIGNER's diff description, plus independent reads of test/support/tenant_fixture_dispatch_test.exs and §9.3 of the design doc itself.

1. MODE-AGNOSTIC RESTATEMENT (§11.2): confirmed. The 'Purpose' paragraph no longer frames the goal only around {:shared, self()}; it now says the goal is reusing 'the SAME connection the caller's own test process is already using at the moment this function runs — whatever mode that connection is under'. The load-bearing 'Concrete mechanism' step 3 paragraph was rewritten from 'the caller's own {:shared, self()} mode ... is left completely alone' to 'since this path issues no Sandbox.mode/2 call itself, whichever mode/connection the caller's test process is ALREADY using at the moment this function runs is left completely undisturbed' — this is exactly the mode-agnostic property step-07b required, stated as the PRIMARY claim, not a caveat appended after the fact.

2. MODE-AGNOSTIC RESTATEMENT (§11.4): confirmed. A new bullet was added asking 'Does §11.2's safety hold for a caller whose ambient mode is :auto rather than {:shared, self()} ... ?' and answering 'Yes, but not via the {:shared, self()} property ... because the property that actually matters is mode-agnostic: this path disturbs nothing, so whichever mode/connection was already ambient stays ambient.' The Conclusion paragraph was likewise extended to state both properties side by side rather than only the {:shared, self()} one.

3. tenant_fixture_dispatch_test.exs NAMED AS THE CONCRETE :auto INSTANCE: confirmed in both §11.2 and §11.4. §11.2's Purpose paragraph and mechanism step 3 both name the file and quote its line-60 `setup do Sandbox.mode(Letflow.Repo, :auto) end`, stating it runs after DataCase's injected setup and before provisioned_tenant!/1. §11.4's new bullet repeats this by name with the same line-60 citation. Independently re-read test/support/tenant_fixture_dispatch_test.exs directly (not taken from the design's quote): line 51 is `use Letflow.DataCase, async: false`, and lines 59-62 are exactly `setup do\n  Sandbox.mode(Letflow.Repo, :auto)\n  :ok\nend` — the design's quotation is accurate, not fabricated or misquoted.

4. §9.3 CITATION FOR THE :auto SUB-CASE: confirmed as substantively correct, not just present. Independently re-read §9.3 (lines 731-789) directly: its steps 3-4 trace exactly the property being cited — under :auto mode, a lone test process's first post-mode-flip query auto-checks-out a fresh proxy and is recorded as that proxy's owner (`manager.ex:279`, `Map.put(checkouts, caller, {:owner, ref, proxy})`), and every subsequent query from the same process reuses that same proxy via the `{status, _ref, proxy} when status in [:owner, :allowed]` clause. This is precisely 'single owner reusing one connection under :auto', which is what §11.2/§11.4's new text claims §9.3 establishes — the citation is accurate, the mechanism it points to genuinely supports the conclusion, and this is not a citation to a section that only superficially resembles the needed property.

5. SPOT-CHECK — §11.1/§11.3/§11.5/§11.6/§11.7/§11.8 unmodified beyond claim: confirmed via `git show 75184403 -- lib/letflow/design/iss0113-tenant-fixture-sandbox-restore-opt-in.md | grep '^@@'`. Exactly four hunks: (a) lines 1-7, the top status header; (b)+(c) lines 2175-2231, both inside §11.2's own span (2184-2266, confirmed via a fresh grep of `^### 11\.` section markers — §11.1 ends at 2183, §11.2.1 starts at 2267); (d) lines 2422-2470, inside §11.4's own span (2400-2493, §11.5 starts at 2494). No hunk overlaps §11.1 (2089-2183), §11.3 (2354-2399), §11.5 (2494-2545), §11.6 (2546-2589), §11.7 (2590-2677), or §11.8 (2678-end). The spot-check independently confirms step-07c's own claim rather than accepting it on the producer's word.

6. NO IMPLEMENTATION CODE / NO NEW DEFERRALS: all four diff hunks are prose only — no fenced code block (```) added or removed by this commit; the file's existing 10 fenced blocks (all pre-existing, all inside §3/§9/§10, none inside §11) are unaffected. No 'TBD' or new OQ marker introduced — §11.8's open-questions list is untouched per the hunk-range check above.

All acceptance criteria for this focused re-gate are met. The correction is textually accurate against every source it cites (the test file's actual content, §9.3's actual trace) and does not merely restate the producer's claim — each citation was independently re-verified against the underlying artefact. §11 as a whole (§11.0-§11.8) now passes cleanly across both gate iterations; nothing further blocks implementation.
